comparator.name: Bachelor Taalwetenschap
comparator.sourceNotes: The current curriculum for students starting in 2026 defines a 180-EC bachelor comprising a 120-EC major and 60 EC of electives. The major contains two 30-EC first-year core profiles, one 30-EC specialisation, two compulsory methodology courses totalling 15 EC, a 7.5-EC capstone/preparatory course and a 7.5-EC BA thesis. The generic normalized target does not name a specialisation. Language and Cognition is selected because the programme overview defines Linguistics through how people speak and understand one another, how language works, language acquisition and processing in the brain; the selected package most broadly develops those defining questions without narrowing the route to Dutch-language society or computation. All eight first-year courses, both compulsory second-year methodology courses, the four-course Language and Cognition package, capstone, thesis and the complete 60-EC open elective space are represented. This route was fixed before UCR fit was assessed.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The generic target offers three specialisations. Language and Cognition best represents the programme’s broad defining questions about how people speak and understand one another, how language is acquired and how the brain processes language. It was selected independently of UCR fit; Taal en Samenleving and Language and Computation remain separately evidenced directions for UCR alternatives.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest match owns the broad structural, cognitive, acquisition, meaning and communication evidence. Language, Society and Communication and Language, Computation and AI are included sequentially because each is an official, independently evidenced specialisation direction, can be implemented coherently at UCR and differs materially from the preceding alternative. All generator-eligible interests 16239–16258 are assigned either to the closest-match core or one of these two candidates. The three schedules contain exactly 24 courses/180 EC, satisfy prerequisite and semester availability constraints, include at least six level-300 courses and are pairwise distinct by substantially more than 30 EC.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Introduction to Brain & Behavior provides a broad cognitive and behavioural foundation for the psychology of language.
Style & Meaning directly analyses how linguistic choices produce meaning in context.
Statistics & Experimental Methods directly supports empirical design and quantitative analysis.
Lifespan Developmental Psychology contributes evidence about cognitive development relevant to language acquisition.
Advanced Research Seminar provides advanced research synthesis and design experience, while not constituting the comparator capstone itself.
Psycholinguistics directly studies language acquisition, comprehension and production using psychology and neuroscience.
No scheduled UCR course reproduces the specific From Language to Linguistics component.
No scheduled UCR course reproduces the specific Comparative Morphosyntax component.
No scheduled UCR course reproduces the specific Phonetics component.
No scheduled UCR course reproduces the specific The Grammar of Words component.
No scheduled UCR course reproduces the specific Semantics and Pragmatics component.
No scheduled UCR course reproduces the specific Language Acquisition and Language Structure component.
No scheduled UCR course reproduces the specific Sociolinguistics component.
Introduction to Data Science includes text data, data cleaning and visual analysis relevant to digital language research.
No scheduled UCR course reproduces the specific Phonology and Fieldwork component.
The comparator requires an independent bachelor thesis; no scheduled UCR course is a thesis.
The comparator’s genuine 60-EC open elective space is preserved rather than claimed against fixed UCR courses.

notes.text: Utrecht Linguistics has a fixed 120-EC major with one 30-EC specialisation and 60 EC of genuine elective space. UCR uses a fully specified 24-course liberal-arts curriculum; the comparison preserves the comparator’s open elective space rather than inventing subjects for it.

UCR offers relevant psycholinguistics, communication, cognition, data and AI courses but no full sequence in phonetics, phonology, morphosyntax and formal linguistics, and no scheduled course is a BA thesis. These gaps remain explicit.
